title: Cross-SDK adaptive circuit + cost-aware retry defaults and streaming dedupe ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Clients across Python/TypeScript/Go currently have divergent sensible defaults for retries, backoff, and stream resumption. This causes inconsistent user experiences, operational load, and cost surprises. Goal: Provide a cross-SDK opinionated defaults bundle that (1) is safe for production, (2) is cost-aware (per-request token budget), (3) supports streaming semantics with deduplication/resume ergonomics, and (4) supplies an adaptive circuit-breaker to avoid cascading failures. This ticket defines defaults, example usage, and an implementation + rollout plan for SDKs.
decision_record: We will adopt an adaptive circuit-breaker combined with a per-request retry budget expressed as a fraction of expected token cost. Default backoff will be exponential with full jitter and a capped elapsed time window. Idempotency keys will be recommended as high-entropy UUIDv7 by default; SDKs will provide a small helper generator with deterministic options for user-supplied ids. Streaming dedupe will use a sliding hash window (default 120s) and resume tokens for stream continuation. These choices balance safety and ergonomics while keeping costs predictable.
defaults:
Default parameters (applies unless user overrides):

- Global model: conservative-by-default to protect Hosted tenants and recommend looser settings for Dedicated.

Python defaults: base_backoff_ms=100, max_backoff_ms=4000, max_attempts=4, jitter=full, per_request_retry_budget=0.25 (fraction of estimated token cost), circuit_window_s=60, circuit_failure_threshold=0.2 (20% failure rate), circuit_min_requests=10, idempotency_ttl_s=86400, stream_dedupe_window_s=120, stream_resume_grace_s=30

TypeScript defaults: base_backoff_ms=100, max_backoff_ms=4500, max_attempts=4, jitter=full, per_request_retry_budget=0.20, circuit_window_s=45, circuit_failure_threshold=0.25, circuit_min_requests=8, idempotency_ttl_s=86400, stream_dedupe_window_s=90, stream_resume_grace_s=30

Go defaults: base_backoff_ms=80, max_backoff_ms=3500, max_attempts=5 (allow one extra for low-latency networks), jitter=full, per_request_retry_budget=0.30, circuit_window_s=75, circuit_failure_threshold=0.18, circuit_min_requests=12, idempotency_ttl_s=86400, stream_dedupe_window_s=150, stream_resume_grace_s=45

Notes: per_request_retry_budget is interpreted by SDKs using local token-estimator heuristics (based on prompt length + expected continuation length). SDKs should surface a meter for consumed retry budget when tracing is enabled.
example_snippets:
Python usage:

from redwood_sdk import Client, RetryConfig
client = Client(retry=RetryConfig())  # uses conservative defaults including cost-aware budget

# opt-out: one-line override
client = Client(retry=RetryConfig(max_attempts=2, per_request_retry_budget=0.0))

TypeScript usage:

import { Redwood, RetryConfig } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ retry: new RetryConfig() })

// stream with automatic dedupe and resume
const stream = client.chat.stream({ messages, onMessage: m => console.log(m) })

Go usage (pseudo):

cli := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithRetry(redwood.DefaultRetry()))
resp, err := cli.Generate(ctx, req)

The SDK helper will expose utilities: GenerateIdempotencyKey(uuidv7=true), InspectRetryBudget(resp.Trace), StreamResumeToken(stream.Handle)
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) implement defaults and expose opt-out knobs
SDKs provide idempotency key helper and document recommended TTL
Streaming clients perform local dedupe with configurable window and resume token semantics
Automated integration tests prove no >2x spike in hosted token consumption under realistic traffic when defaults enabled
Circuit-breaker raises metrics and prevents repeated hammering under 5 minute failure bursts
implementation_steps: Design SDK retry budget estimator interface (shared spec)
Implement circuit-breaker primitives in each SDK using shared behavior (windowed failure rate, min requests, cooldown)
Add idempotency key helper and default generator with configurable entropy
Implement sliding-window streaming dedupe with hash cache and resume token support
Add tracing hooks: emit retry_budget_used, circuit_state, dedupe_events
Add unit and integration tests, load test against hosted sandbox
Docs + changelog + migration guide for customers
qa_checks: Unit tests for retry/backoff behavior including jitter distribution
Integration tests that simulate transient 503/502 with token cost accounting
Fuzz tests for stream resume tokens and dedupe correctness
Load test to compare token consumption with older SDK version under same workload
Verify metrics emitted to Console: sdk.retry.attempts, sdk.circuit.state, sdk.dedupe.hits
risks_mitigation: Risk: aggressive defaults could increase customer latency or token consumption. Mitigation: conservative default (low attempts, small budget fraction), opt-out flags, and rollout to Hosted as opt-in feature flag for first 2 weeks. Risk: cross-SDK behavioral drift. Mitigation: shared spec and a compatibility test-suite run in CI. Risk: resume tokens leaking sensitive prompt context — ensure resume tokens are opaque handles referencing server-side state or local stable checkpoints, and document potential privacy constraints.

notes: Follow-on work: provide server-side advisory endpoints that return tuned per-customer retry budgets based on account tier and recent traffic patterns. We will monitor token-unit delta after rollout and keep a migration toggle for Hosted customers for 30 days. Consider offering a 'developer-mode' with more permissive retry defaults for faster iteration during prototyping.
